description: Single source of truth for CI/local-runner gate names and status (AUDIT-27 CI-08). scripts/verify-ci-docs-drift.py enforces that docs/ci-pipeline.md, .github/workflows/*.yml, scripts/check.sh, and scripts/check-ui.mjs all agree with this file. Adding a gate here is the ONLY way to add a gate; renaming/removing one here (plus its runner/CI declarations) is the only way to remove it.

gates.label: UI unit tests
gates._note: Was ci.yml#ui-test. dev-ci.yml#ui-test runs `cd ui && npm test` (vitest) -- the same suite under the same job name.

gates._note: Was ci.yml#go. gofmt/go vet/go test -short now run in dev-ci.yml#static-gates, verified green locally first. The pre-commit Go gate remains the only place Go is enforced on a commit.

gates._note: Was website.yml#check. dev-ci.yml#website runs `cd website && npm test`; website.yml is .bak.

gates._note: Was ci.yml#rust-test-fast. dev-ci.yml runs `cargo nextest run --workspace --all-features` with NO excludes, so it covers this more broadly than check.sh, whose own nextest step excludes oz-pos-app. nextest does not run doctests, so that part remains check.sh-only.

gates._note: Was ci.yml#rust-money-format. Runs in dev-ci.yml#static-gates, verified green locally.

gates._note: Was ci.yml#skill-drift-tests. Runs in dev-ci.yml#static-gates, verified green locally.

gates.label: Panic inventory
gates._note: Was ci.yml#rust-panic-inventory, then had no CI job at all while scan-unwrap-panic.py was red. R36-12 found the redness was the SCANNER's bug -- it did not track /* */ block comments across lines, so it read the repo's audit stamps as code (6 false positives) and, in apps/cloud-server/src/redirect.rs, treated a stamp mentioning #[cfg(test)] as the start of test code and stopped checking the rest of the file (1 suppressed real finding). Fixed, triaged, and now enforced in dev-ci.yml#static-gates.

gates.label: CI docs drift
gates._note: History worth keeping: this was declared 'required' while pointing at ci.yml#ci-docs-drift, a workflow retired to .bak by 23c96330, so it enforced nothing anywhere and the status was false. It was downgraded to 'advisory' when first wired into dev-ci.yml because the checker was reporting 68 items it had no vocabulary for. R36-10 closed those out to 0 and the step is now blocking -- the stated condition. advisory_at is removed because the step no longer sets continue-on-error. Two steps in each runner since 0.0.37: the drift check, and `--self-test`, which mutates four of the classifiers this gate depends on and requires each to be noticed, plus a control that must still pass. It exists because this is the gate that polices every other gate's CI claim and was the only one of the family without one, so "drift: 0 items" was indistinguishable from "the checker stopped looking" -- the failure that let the manifest rot. `ci.steps` is a list because the job has two relevant steps; singular `step` is only read by the advisory_at == "step" path.

steps: Verify CI docs agree with gates.json and the workflows

gates.label: Fuzz
gates._note: cargo-fuzz ran in ci.yml#fuzz only. The RUSTC_WRAPPER='' note recorded below is still accurate for whoever restores it.
gates.note: The fuzz job deliberately sets RUSTC_WRAPPER: '' in its job env. The ubuntu runner image globally wraps rustc with sccache, which breaks cargo-fuzz's --target build (its rustc version probe execs the resolved nightly toolchain path directly and dies with 'could not execute process sccache .../bin/rustc -vV'). The fuzz job is the only job affected (nightly + --target), so sccache must stay disabled there — do NOT re-add it. Caching is instead handled by Swatinem/rust-cache@v2 with `workspaces: fuzz` (cargo-fuzz builds into fuzz/target/, which default workspace discovery misses).

gates.label: Release version gate
gates._note: Added 0.0.37: the gate existed in both runners and had no record here, which is the exact blind spot this manifest exists to close -- its own description says adding a gate here is the ONLY way to add a gate, yet check.sh:245 (`step "release version gate"`) and dev-ci.yml#release-readiness were both already invoking `node scripts/check-release-version.mjs --self-test`. Found while building a CI-side analogue of hook_step_orphans; the three other candidates it surfaced were false positives from matching runner labels by exact key instead of the substring containment has_needle() actually uses. Nothing in the existing checker could have reported this: hook_step_orphans scans the pre-commit hook, not check.sh, and the runners-vocabulary check only validates labels that are already declared. Ships with --self-test so a regression cannot silently turn it into a no-op.

gates.label: Release workflow validation
gates._note: R36-11. release.yml was renamed to release.yml.bak by 23c96330 with an empty commit message and nothing replaced it, so pushing a v* tag produced no installers for a whole release cycle. A workflow that never runs cannot report its own breakage, so this validates statically what needs no tag, key material, or macOS/Windows runner: action pins, referenced paths, docker residue left by the desktop-only restore, an inventory gate demanding an artifact no matrix entry builds, and that a missing UPDATER_PRIVATE_KEY still hard-fails rather than publishing an unsigned manifest every client rejects. Ships with --self-test (8 mutations) so a regression cannot silently turn it into a no-op.

gates.label: Release readiness
gates._note: Runs scripts/check-updater-compat.mjs, which builds a Rust harness pinned to the minisign-verify version the real Tauri updater client uses and proves that signatures from generate-latest-json.mjs VERIFY, that a tampered installer is REJECTED, and that the pubkey committed in tauri.conf.json parses. Before this it ran ONLY inside release.yml.bak, i.e. nowhere at all -- so the signing chain could have rotted silently alongside the retired workflow and the first symptom would be customers unable to auto-update. Path-gated on the release toolchain and the updater pubkey because the harness needs a cold cargo build. No `runners` key: that field names LOCAL entry points, and this one needs a cargo build, so it is CI-only.

gates.label: Doc uniqueness
gates._note: Added in 0.0.36 after f3d9cca6 moved the repo-root subscription-tiers.md into docs/records/ without noticing docs/guides/ already had a copy from 28147fe4, leaving two tracked files both stamped 'single source of truth' for pricing with disagreeing entitlement rows. No gate compared documents to each other, so nothing saw it. Local-only for now: it carries a pair-specific baseline for that one unresolved finding (R36-14, needs a product decision because white-label has no runtime entitlement check to adjudicate against), and a gate with a live baseline should earn CI-blocking status after the baseline is empty, the same condition R36-10 set for ci-docs-drift. --self-test and the 5-case harness both pass.

gates.label: EOL guard
gates._note: Added in 0.0.36 (R36-15). The pre-commit line-ending step filtered on 'git check-attr text' alone, which is wrong twice: it ignored '.gitattributes *.bat text eol=crlf' and stripped CRLF from the working tree (producing a phantom-dirty git status with zero content diff), and because '* text=auto' reports 'auto' for every path including binaries, a staged PNG had the 0D 0A in its signature deleted and the mangled blob re-staged -- verified on apps/desktop-client/icons/32x32.png, 1515 to 1507 bytes. Both are silent corruption behind a green hook. The test extracts the live guard from .githooks/pre-commit rather than copying it, so it cannot drift from what it polices, and it fails loudly if either guard disappears.

gates.label: AGENTS.md mirror truthfulness
gates._note: Added in 0.0.36. Three copies of the agent rules exist (root AGENTS.md, .agents/AGENTS.md, .prime/AGENTS.md) and scripts/bump-version.ps1 syncs only their version lines -- the file itself documents that nothing syncs the gate list. Twice in this release a mirror stated something the repo contradicted: .agents/AGENTS.md kept saying 'Steps 6, 7 and 8 have no CI backstop' after 13f2a1dc put Go into dev-ci.yml#static-gates, and root AGENTS.md claimed dev-ci 'runs on every PR and push' when it has no push trigger at all. The first is the mirror that governs work under .agents/, so an agent following it would believe Go changes are unguarded. Required and CI-blocking from day one, unlike ci-docs-drift, because it has no baseline and no pre-existing failures: ground truth is read from .githooks/pre-commit, .github/workflows/*.yml and Cargo.toml rather than asserted, so adding a gate or bumping the version updates the expectation without touching the checker. --self-test mutates each mirror and requires a named finding; a mutation that changes nothing is reported WRONG rather than passing silently, which is how the .prime phrasing gap was found and closed.

gates.label: Conventional-commit subjects
gates._note: Added in 0.0.36. .githooks/commit-msg has enforced the subject format locally since 9cf14190, but core.hooksPath is set by setup-dev.ps1 and is not versioned, so a clone that skips setup gets no subject gate -- a limitation the hook's own header states and defers to a future CI check. This closes that. The rule is extracted from the hook at run time (TYPES, PATTERN, and the Merge/Revert/fixup/squash/amend exemptions) rather than duplicated, so local and CI cannot drift into disagreeing about what is legal; each extractor raises rather than returning an empty set, because an empty exemption list would reject every merge commit and an empty type list would accept anything. Commits older than the hook's own introduction are skipped, derived via `git log --diff-filter=A -- .githooks/commit-msg` rather than a hardcoded sha, and the skipped count is printed so the grandfathering is visible. Verified against the four commits the hook header names as its motivation (2eea3d07, faa5dae0, 5855c429, 84a71f3e): all four are found, all four are pre-rule, and the 77 commits since the hook conform. The CI step needs fetch-depth 0 -- with the default depth of 1 the range is empty and the gate would pass by checking nothing.

gates.label: PG schema drift guard
gates._note: Added in 0.0.37. 20260813_init.pg.sql is GENERATED by this script from the SQLite migrations and must never be hand-edited. The job lived in ci.yml, which 23c96330 renamed to .bak with no replacement, and it was restored neither in dev-ci.yml nor in check.sh -- so the only guard was pre-commit step 7, and core.hooksPath is set by scripts/setup-dev.ps1 and is not versioned. On a clone that skips setup, a stale or hand-edited generated file committed and merged clean. `--check` is a pure text comparison: no Docker, no psycopg, no sqlite handle, ~1s. Note the asymmetry this closes is not that the gate was weak, but that it had NO gates.json record at all, so verify-ci-docs-drift.py could not report a gate that is required but not enforced -- it never learned the gate existed.

gates.label: Migration column types
gates._note: Added in 0.0.37. Exact-decimal columns must be fixed-point integers (*_minor / *_millionths); a new float needs a justified whitelist entry, because a float money column is the defect class this repo's Money struct exists to prevent. Same history as pg-schema-drift: retired with ci.yml, never restored anywhere but the opt-in hook. Run here WITHOUT --staged-only, which is what the hook uses -- CI must scan all 28 migration files, not whatever one commit happened to touch, or a float column shipped by a hook-less clone is never revisited. ~0.1s.

gates.label: i18n bundle parity
gates._note: Added in 0.0.37. This is pre-commit step 4 and had NO gates.json record until then, which is a worse failure than pointing at a retired workflow: verify-ci-docs-drift.py iterates the gates present in the manifest, so a gate with no record can never be reported as required-but-not-enforced. The blind spot is structural, not a data error. It is also the step whose own history is the worst -- before the Fluent page audit it walked only literal <Localized id> under ui/src/features/** and skipped every shared-chrome and context file it was handed, so 14 broken keys shipped while it reported clean. --scan-dirs is load-bearing: the tool defaults to `features` alone, and the six directories add 108 files (228 -> 336, 47% more coverage). A runner that omits the flag prints '0 missing key(s)' over a third of the surface unexamined. CI and check.sh deliberately run WITHOUT --staged-only, which the hook uses: a key reference shipped by a hook-less clone must be revisited by something.

gates.label: Runner label integrity
gates._note: Added in 0.0.37. verify-ci-docs-drift.py checked each gate's `runners` labels with has_needle(), which is ANY-of: a gate declaring three labels was satisfied by one. Deleting the other two from check.sh left the manifest asserting guards that no longer existed while the checker printed '0 drift item(s)'. Demonstrated against this repo's own ci-docs-drift gate, which declares both 'ci docs drift' and 'ci docs drift self-test' -- removing the self-test step changed nothing. The rule is now missing_needles(), which reports every label matching nothing; adopting it was safe precisely because the manifest was accurate under the stricter reading (all 5 multi-label gates resolved every label), so this closed a latent gap rather than converting it into false failures. Two properties the test encodes because both produced confident wrong answers first: ROOT derives from __file__ not cwd, so a fixture that omits the checker itself reads the real repo and agrees with itself; and needles match by substring, so a short label cannot fail while a longer one containing it exists.
